findings.summary: the unroll-budget fold machinery was built twice — the uniformity comparison and the repeat-loop emitter verbatim in `emitBudgetedStaticIndexIterations` and `emitStaticHandleTableForOf` — while the third static unroller (the array-literal `for...of`) got the budget push with no fold arm at all; one `capturesAreIdentical` + `emitRepeatedTemplate` beside the shared `emitCapturedIterations` now serves all three, with the literal unroller riding the same budget-triggered fold (no corpus scene currently reaches it, proven byte-identical over all 218)

the once-emitted-method arm restated the free-function machinery three times over — `resolveMethodSignature` copied `resolveSignature`'s ~60-line data-signature mapping (the two copies already disagreed on `carriesFunction` returns), `emitMethodDefinition` restated `captureDataFunctionBody`'s binding/scope protocol, `ensureMethodEmitted` cloned `ensureEmitted` — plus a never-read `MethodFieldChannel.declaration` field; one `mapDataSignature` with the method arm's two deltas as declared inputs, shared body-capture hooks, one parameterized `ensureEmitted`, field dropped; quake/doom/racer byte-identical

the golden fixed-frame rule (`referenceFrame`, else the retained-UI full-page `BBLITE_SCREENSHOT_FRAME` fallback) lived twice — `instrumentedReferenceFrame` and `runSceneParity`'s inline derivation, held equal only by a comment, the exact drift class the instrumented-capture fix had just closed; one exported `goldenFixedFrame` in parity-scene.ts now serves both, the pinning test reads the canonical copy

typed-array-literal hoistability was decided by regexing emitted C++ (`NUMERIC_LITERAL_TEXT` over `compileNumber` output) — the repo's own named read-back-out-of-emitted-code trap; both call sites hold the structural fact, so the array-literal site now derives it per element via `staticNumberValue` and the tuple site passes its already-proven flag; regex deleted, corpus byte-identical

the full-surface `clearRect` proof's third route crossed two compilation-global axis sets, so with canvases 300x200 and 400x100 recorded, `clearRect(0,0,300,100)` passed while matching neither; sizes are now recorded as (width,height) pairs keyed by a minted per-canvas id that propagates like `uiCanvas` itself (keying by the element's cpp was tried and is unsound — canvas and context materialize as different locals), and the two-canvas cross case refuses under a new test

the UI style audit and the projection derived three combination predicates independently (gradient-text clip, gradient background, display:grid pairing) and segmented declaration lists with different splitters (paren-aware walk vs paren-blind regex); the predicates are shared statics and both parsers now segment through one paren-aware walk, with the projection's rewrites masked over it

the backend-TU sync test regexed `output-projection.ts` source text for path literals although `featureSources` is an exported structural record; it now imports the record, so no spelling of a source entry can dodge the assertion

Dawn's destructor gained three byte-identical 18-line variant-family release sequences and SDL two copied pipeline-map release loops; one file-local `release_variant_family` (concrete types — a template added nothing) and one local lambda now serve them in release order

the standalone render-capture gate was spelled six times across the sprite/effect/frame-graph drivers (the frame-graph pair added the fifth and sixth copies while the branch was editing the gate's own state holder); `CaptureGate::maybe_write_standalone_render_capture` folds all six to one-liners

Dawn's new whole-function try/catch duplicated the normal exit's teardown verbatim and its `ui_runtime.reset()` was redundant under unwinding; a shared RAII `PickHookGuard` now clears the hook on both backends, Dawn's wrapper is deleted, SDL's catch keeps only what the guard does not cover

the sprite dirty-range resolution (full-upload derivation, min-clamps, consumed-range stamp) had become byte-identical in both backend headers after the recovery-guard unification; `resolve_sprite_dirty_range`/`mark_sprite_dirty_range_consumed` in the shared header now own it, only the backend write call stays local

the CPU-profile startup mark and `[cpu][frame]` line format were verbatim cross-backend copies; one shared `CpuStartupMark` + `print_cpu_frame_profile` (label and optional `write_ms` parameters) keeps the format contract in one file, output byte-identical to a parser

the shared event-drain helper stopped short of the two scene renderers, leaving the poll contract in three spellings; a per-event dispatched hook now carries the camera-pointer arm and both scene TUs ride the helper, with the architecture test pinning the converged shape

`apply_canvas_cursor` ran per surviving event inside the shared drain (tens to hundreds of times per frame under pointer motion, and newly extended to two drivers); it now runs once after the drain when any event was dispatched — identical end-of-batch cursor state

the disposed-render-texture refusal walk re-ran every frame forever per disposed record; the suggested cached triggers were proven unsound against a layer registered after dispose+release, so the sound cheapest form landed instead — one union walk per sync, run only when a disposed record exists (zero walks in the common case, one instead of R with disposals)

the hardened missing-array-value slot re-defaulted on every miss including through the const accessors, turning the normal guarded-read miss path into construct/assign/destroy churn for struct and string elements; the const overloads now read an immutable `static const` default and only the mutable overload keeps the resetting slot its threat model needs
`stripKeywordOutsideLiterals` parsed every unasynced pinned module twice (once per keyword); one parse with a combined disjoint-match replace now serves both keywords

camera-lowerer's `requireArcAccumulation` and `requireAssignment` were near-twin closures (filter pinned assignments by operator+path, assert the right side's shape) differing in list, error node and strictness; one private `requirePinnedWrite` with those as parameters serves both anchor blocks

the bake-cache test file carried the NODE_TEST_CONTEXT lift/restore juggling twice (sync and async helpers, whose restore timing genuinely differs); a shared `liftCacheMarker` core now owns the env handling and each wrapper keeps only its timing
compiling the retained-canvas size RHS once instead of twice
